page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is relatively robust, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2149.0 and an average stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1942.19. However, due to the physical limitation of a single core, multi-core performance is constrained, as evidenced by a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2641.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core score of 1991.97. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached large-block read and write speeds registering at 21.51 GB/sec and 14.04 GB/sec respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E2s_v6 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its low vCPU count, making it a viable option for workloads that require a larger memory footprint without demanding heavy parallel processing power. It is well-suited for lightweight database operations, caching layers, basic web serving, and single-threaded applications. However, the lack of local storage and weak multi-threaded performance make it less suitable for intensive compilation, heavy data science jobs, or highly parallelized enterprise workloads.
